title: Process worker and SQLite durability
summary: Bounded Windows process-tree kill behavior, added local worker child heartbeats/stale-slot reclaim, and added best-effort SQLite mirror maintenance.
reason: Unattended control paths cannot rely on external process tools, worker children, or SQLite WAL state staying healthy for 30 days without timeout evidence and recovery hooks.
behavior_before: A Windows taskkill hang could block process cleanup, worker slots lacked child heartbeat evidence, and SQLite mirror maintenance was not opportunistically tracked after writes.
behavior_after: Process cleanup returns bounded degraded evidence on taskkill timeout, worker slots can reclaim stale heartbeat children, and state DB maintenance runs best-effort on interval or WAL threshold.
manual_validation: PowerShell parser check for changed process/queue/status entrypoint scripts - passed
rollback_plan: Revert kill timeout, heartbeat, stale slot reclaim, and SQLite maintenance changes plus tests; JSON state remains authoritative and no source/output files require migration.
notes: Bound process-tree kill timeout, worker heartbeat evidence, stale slot reclaim, and SQLite maintenance.
